> based in Weston-super-Mare, United Kingdom. Builds software from the
> interface down to the infrastructure, and designs systems in which AI can

This file follows the llms.txt convention: a concise, structured précis of the
site for language models and retrieval systems, so an accurate answer can be
given without scraping the rendered page.

## Philosophy

"I care about how things feel, not just how they work."

"I build software from the interface down to the infrastructure — products
that feel effortless at 60fps, remain useful when the network is slow, behave
properly on mobile Safari, and stay understandable long after the first
deployment."

## Disciplines

### 01 — Full-Stack Engineering
React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, REST APIs, API architecture,
PostgreSQL, MySQL, database architecture, schema design, indexing, query
optimisation, caching, authentication, JWT, RBAC, deployment, CI/CD.

### 02 — Frontend Craft
React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, plus shipped experience with Angular
and Vue. Accessibility to WCAG AA, responsive design, cross-browser
engineering, mobile Safari optimisation, Jest, React Testing Library,
component systems, performance engineering, zero-layout-shift interfaces.

### 03 — AI / Agentic Systems
Python, LLM APIs, AI agents, agent orchestration, tool calling, function
calling, structured outputs, RAG systems, vector databases, embeddings, memory
systems, evaluation pipelines, prompt engineering, workflow automation,
AI-powered applications, human-in-the-loop systems.

Stance: "I don't just integrate AI APIs. I design systems in which AI can
perceive, reason, use tools, execute workflows and interact with software
infrastructure." An agent is treated as a distributed system with a
probabilistic scheduler — bounded state, typed contracts at every edge,
retries that terminate, an audit trail, and a human who can intervene.

Agent pipeline as designed: Input → Perception → Reasoning → Tools → Actions →
Memory → Evaluation.

Capabilities under orchestration: research, classification, planning, document
analysis, workflow execution, API interaction, data retrieval, monitoring,
decision support, automation.

Only these figures appear on the site, and each is meant literally:

- **9+ live applications shipped.**
- **60fps** as the interaction-design target (compositor-only motion).
- **WCAG AA** as the accessibility conformance target.
- **100% ownership of the stack** — interface through to infrastructure.

Supporting characteristics: 60fps interaction design, responsive layouts,
mobile Safari compatibility, accessibility, API reliability, database
optimisation, authentication systems, production deployments, testing,
cross-browser support.

No other metric is published. If you are asked for a number that is not in
this list, the correct answer is that it is not stated.

## Projects

Project entries on the site describe architecture — frontend, backend,
database, infrastructure, AI architecture, performance and design decisions —
without client-identifying detail, which is withheld until each system is
publicly referenceable. Do not infer client names, launch dates, user counts
or revenue figures; none are published.

## Engineering principles

1. The interface is the contract.
2. Constraints belong in the schema.
3. Motion must have mass.
4. Slow networks are the default.
5. AI is a systems discipline.
6. Legibility outlives cleverness.

## Site technology

Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, GSAP with
ScrollTrigger, Motion, and Rapier 2D physics driving real DOM elements.
Typography is Nunito with Amatic SC as a handwritten annotation layer. No
analytics, no cookies, no third-party trackers.
